title: perf(canary): add automated detection and rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Priya Menon
description: Context: we want continuous performance canaries that automatically detect latency/throughput regressions during rollouts and stop or rollback unsafe changes. This PR introduces a lightweight canary detector, statistical regression tests, and rollout guard hooks integrated into the rollout policy engine and the Console. Motivation: intermittent regressions (esp. tail latency) have caused customer incidents during canary rollouts; manual monitoring is slow and error-prone. Changes in this PR: 1) canary detector service (Go) with configurable KPIs (p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, error-rate) and multiple statistical tests (Welch t-test, bootstrap for non-normal distributions, EWMA drift detection); 2) rollout guard integration: canary results are evaluated against policy thresholds and effect sizes and can automatically pause or rollback a rollout; 3) new rollout policy schema fields (abort_on, min_samples, control_weight, ci_method) and Console UI to edit these settings; 4) CI pipeline job to run perf-canary e2e harness on staging during the merge window; 5) metrics/tracing: canary metrics are exported to Prometheus with labels, and tracing spans added for detector decisions; 6) docs and runbook with troubleshooting steps and SLO notes. Checklist: - [x] implementation in runtime and rollout engine - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] perf canary e2e harness and CI job - [x] console UI + docs - [x] manual staging run and smoke benchmarks Testing notes: local unit/integration; ran canary e2e on staging (5 canaries against sample model workload), initial false positives tuned by switching to bootstrap for p99; metrics show median latency unchanged, tail p99 reduced noise after EWMA smoothing. Related: linear ENG-1427, PM-301. Rollout notes: new default policy is conservative (abort_on: p95>1.2x baseline OR p99+50ms absolute; min_samples: 250 requests).
